name: marcella lemon celery
instructions: braise celery, potatoes, olive oil, salt, lemon in a shallow pool of water until the water evaporates. serve.
notes:
marcella hazan. peel the fibers off the back of the celery first.

CELERY IS MANDATORY — IT'S THE MAIN LEMON PAIRING: celery is the load-bearing ingredient here; it's what the lemon is actually pairing with. Potatoes and green beans are supporting starches/vegetables, but the celery-and-lemon axis is the dish. Don't drop celery.

GREEN BEANS (SECONDARY) — WORK ALONGSIDE OR IN PLACE OF POTATOES: green beans braise well in the same shallow-pool-of-water format and slot in as another vegetable component. Use alongside potatoes for more variety, or in place of potatoes if you want a lighter version.

IF YOU FORGO POTATOES, USE LESS LEMON: potatoes soak up and mute lemon in a way green beans and celery alone don't. Without the potato buffer there's less starch to distract from the lemon, and the same lemon quantity reads more assertive on the palate. Scale the lemon back when going potato-free.

=== CHICKEN BROTH (SECONDARY) — SWAP WATER WHEN MAKING ALONGSIDE CHICKEN PICCATA ===

Chicken broth (or stock) can be used in place of water for the shallow-pool braise. When to reach for it specifically: making this side ALONGSIDE chicken-piccata — the leftover chicken broth from the piccata pan sauce (before it reduces / gets butter-mounted) is exactly what belongs here. Cook the two dishes concurrently and route the broth from one pot to the other.

See CROSS-RECIPE PAIRING below.

=== CROSS-RECIPE PAIRING — CHICKEN-PICCATA ===

This side pairs particularly well with chicken-piccata. The lemon + broth axis matches piccata's sauce base, and the celery + potato + green bean vegetable set fits the 'plated alongside' serving format that piccata wants (see chicken-piccata's NOT A STEW note). You can make both concurrently — the piccata's leftover chicken broth goes into the celery/potato pot as the shallow-pool liquid.
